## Answer
RAG (Retrieve-and-Generate) differs from traditional language models in several ways. Firstly, RAG models do not rely solely on fine-tuning, which is the traditional method of performing a task with a language model. Instead, RAG models can perform tasks with only forward passes at test time, using zero-shot, one-shot, or few-shot settings (Source: data/2005.14165v4.pdf, Page: 6, Figure 2.1). 

Additionally, RAG models can go beyond simple extractive question answering and generate free-form, abstractive text to answer questions (Source: data/2005.11401v4.pdf, Page: 3, §3.2). This is in contrast to traditional language models that may only provide extractive answers.

RAG models also differ from traditional retrieve-and-edit approaches, as they do not focus on lightly editing a retrieved item, but instead aggregate content from several pieces of retrieved content and learn latent retrieval (Source: data/2005.11401v4.pdf, Page: 8).
